what: Mother Wort, an old herb-woman who sells tonics and remedies, painted seriously: a small, wiry old woman of about seventy with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about seven and a half heads tall, a slight stoop at the shoulders. Her face is kindly but sharp: deep wrinkles, a long thin nose, thin lips pressed in a knowing half-smile, shrewd narrowed grey eyes, weather-beaten light tan skin. Her grey hair is pulled back tight into a round bun at the back of her head. She is a living old woman.
colours: a deep emerald-green wool shawl, a long dress of dull dark brown wool, a plain undyed pale sand-beige linen apron, grey hair, weather-beaten light tan face and hands, bunches of dried herbs in straw-brown and dull dark green, pale grey-white cave-moss, one small clear glass bottle of bright green tonic, a mortar bowl of pale grey stone.
wears: She wears a long dark brown wool dress to her ankles, a deep emerald-green wool shawl crossed over her chest and knotted at the front, a plain sand-beige linen apron over the dress, and dark brown leather shoes. From a broad leather belt at her waist hang four bunches of dried herbs tied with string and two tufts of pale grey-white cave-moss, all hanging down against the apron. She has no hat, no hood and a bare head with her grey bun.
holds: She holds exactly two things. In her right hand, held out toward the viewer at chest height a hand's width from her body, one small round glass bottle with a cork, filled with bright green liquid, as big as her fist. In her left hand, held low at her hip, one round stone mortar bowl as big as her two fists, of pale grey stone, with a short stone pestle standing in it.
pose: On two legs, turned three quarters to the viewer, she leans forward a little from a slight stoop, her weight on her front foot and the back heel lifted, as if stepping up to a customer; her right arm reaches out offering the green bottle, her left hand holds the mortar at her hip, her head tilted with a sharp knowing look at the viewer.
must_show: an old woman, wrinkled face, grey hair in a bun
a green shawl over a brown dress and pale apron
bunches of dried herbs hanging from her belt
one small bottle of green tonic held out in one hand
a stone mortar bowl in the other hand

what: Brannoc, a human armourer who forges and sells blades and mail, painted seriously: a broad, strong, grizzled man of about fifty-five with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight heads tall, broad shoulders and very thick muscular forearms. His face is hard-working and stern: a short neat grey beard, a weathered lined brow, a broad nose, steady grey eyes studying the blade, weather-beaten light tan skin with smudges of black soot on his cheek and forearms. His short grey hair is cropped close. He is a living man.
colours: a heavy leather apron the brown of a chestnut, dark scuffed and burned at the hem, a soot-stained off-white linen shirt with the sleeves rolled to the elbow, dark charcoal-grey wool breeches, dark brown boots, weather-beaten light tan skin, grey hair and beard, a hammer of blackened iron, dark gunmetal grey, with bright pale steel-white worn edges and a dark oak handle, a sword blade of bright pale steel-white with a dark gunmetal-grey crossguard.
wears: He wears a soot-stained off-white linen shirt with the sleeves rolled up above the elbows, a heavy chestnut-brown leather smith's apron from his chest to his knees tied at the waist, dark charcoal-grey wool breeches tucked into tall heavy dark brown boots that reach his knees. He has no helmet, no armour, no cloak and a bare head.
holds: He holds exactly two things. In his right hand, gripped near the end of its short dark oak handle and held down beside his right thigh, one heavy smith's hammer with a square block head of blackened iron. Across his flat open left palm, held out level in front of his chest, lies one long straight sword blade of bright pale steel-white with a plain crossguard and a bare tang with no grip, its point toward the left of the picture, its whole length clear against the backdrop.
pose: On two legs, turned three quarters to the viewer, he stands with his feet apart and his weight on his back leg, leaning his head forward and down to squint along the sword blade lying across his left palm, his right arm hanging with the heavy hammer, shoulders squared, as if checking the edge for a flaw.
must_show: a broad grizzled man with a short grey beard
a chestnut-brown leather apron over a soot-stained shirt, sleeves rolled
thick bare forearms
a heavy smith's hammer in one hand
a long bright sword blade laid across the other palm

what: Aldous Vellum, a scribe who sells books and scrolls, painted seriously: a thin, bony, stooped man of about forty-five with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight heads tall, narrow shoulders. His face is long and earnest with a long human nose, bright red and sore at the tip from a bad cold, the reddest thing on his face: round wire spectacles on the nose, mild watery brown eyes, untidy thin brown hair sticking out over his ears, a long chin, pale light tan skin. A long white feather quill pen is tucked behind his right ear, its feathered end pointing up above his head. His fingertips are stained black with ink. He is a living man.
colours: a long plain dark brown wool robe, the brown of a chestnut, with many patch pockets of lighter tan-brown leather, a dark brown leather belt, round brass wire spectacles, a long white feather quill pen, a red-tipped nose, black ink stains on the fingers, an old courier's satchel of dark scuffed chestnut leather stuffed with cream parchment scrolls, a thick book with a dark brown leather cover and cream pages.
wears: He wears one long dark brown wool robe to his ankles with a high plain collar, covered with many square patch pockets sewn on the chest, hips and skirt, some with scroll ends and a spare quill sticking out of them, a dark brown leather belt, and dark brown soft boots. Across his body on a strap hangs one old courier's satchel of dark scuffed chestnut leather at his left hip, its flap open, crammed with six rolled cream parchment scrolls, each as thick as a candle, sticking up high out of it. He has no hat, no hood and a bare head.
holds: He holds exactly one thing: one thick open book, as big as his chest, held up high in his left hand beside his left shoulder, its open cream pages turned out to face the viewer, the way a preacher shows a page to a crowd, clear of his face. His right hand is held out toward the book with one ink-blackened finger pointing at the open page, nothing in it.
pose: On two legs, turned three quarters to the viewer, he leans eagerly forward in a short step, one foot ahead of the other and the back heel lifted, holding the open book up high to show its pages and pointing at them; he is not reading it; he looks straight at the viewer over his spectacles with an eager hopeful smile.
must_show: a thin stooped man in a long brown robe with many pockets
round spectacles and a bright red nose
a quill tucked behind one ear
a satchel stuffed with scrolls at his hip
one thick open book held out in both hands

what: Vesper, a dealer in rare and dangerous things from the deep, painted seriously: an eerie, elegant, ageless man of no age at all, tall and slender, with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about eight and a half heads tall. His face is smooth, narrow and handsome in a cold way: cold chalk-grey skin, the grey of a marble statue, a colour no living person has, never living flesh colour, on his face, neck and hands; eyes that are solid black from lid to lid, two glossy black almond shapes with no white in them at all; a thin polite smile with closed lips; high cheekbones; a sharp chin. His glossy black hair is slicked straight back and falls to his shoulders, dark behind his pale face. He is a person, a living gentleman, not a monster.
colours: a long black wool frock coat with a dark charcoal-grey sheen on the folds, a row of big bright silver buttons as big as coins, a high stiff collar lined with bright silver-grey satin, a white shirt cuff at each wrist, cold chalk-grey skin, long black slicked hair, black eyes, one silver ring set with a big stone glowing bright violet, a small box of glossy black lacquer with bright silver corners and a silver clasp.
wears: He wears a long black wool frock coat that reaches below his knees, buttoned to the throat with a single row of six bright silver buttons, its high stiff black collar standing up round his neck to his jaw, narrow white shirt cuffs at the wrists, slim black trousers and polished black boots. He has no hat, no hood, no cape and a bare head.
holds: He holds exactly two things. His right arm is held out to the side at shoulder height, clear of his body and face, and pinched between his finger and thumb he holds up one silver ring with one big violet stone as big as the top joint of his thumb, glowing bright violet, the brightest thing in the picture, its soft glow small and round the stone only, no bigger than his fist, the backdrop all round it. His left hand rests flat on the lid of one small box of glossy black lacquer with bright silver corners and a silver clasp, as big as a book, which he holds against his left hip, the box tucked in the crook of his arm.
pose: On two legs, turned three quarters to the viewer, he steps forward in a long gliding stride, his front knee bent and his back heel lifted, leaning a little forward at the waist in a courteous bow, his head tilted, holding the violet ring up for the viewer to see, his black eyes fixed on the viewer with a thin smile.
must_show: a tall slender pale ash-grey man in a long black coat with silver buttons
a high stiff collar
entirely black eyes, a thin smile
one small glowing violet ring held up between finger and thumb
a small black lacquer box under the other hand

what: Old Mags Thorn, a camp-follower who sells supplies to soldiers on the road, painted seriously: a lean, wiry old woman of about sixty-five with realistic adult proportions, a small head and long limbs, about seven and a half heads tall, tough and weathered, stooped under the weight of her load. Her face is lined and leathery with a squint and a crooked grin, a strong hooked nose, weather-beaten light tan skin, straggling grey hair tied under a dark brown kerchief. A thick white clay pipe is clenched in the corner of her mouth and juts straight out sideways from her face: its stem as thick as her finger and as long as her hand, its round bowl as big as her thumb, bright white against her face and the backdrop. She is a living old woman.
colours: a patched travelling cloak of dull dark brown wool, the brown of wet peat, with big square patches of pale tan and grey, a dark brown kerchief, a dull grey wool dress, dark brown boots, a huge pack of dark scuffed chestnut leather and dull brown canvas, dented brass and blackened iron pots, an unlit iron lantern, a rolled grey blanket, a short bright white clay pipe, a glass bottle of bright red potion with a bronze neck band.
wears: She wears a dull grey wool dress to her shins, a dull dark brown wool travelling cloak, the brown of wet peat, covered in big sewn-on square patches of pale tan and grey, thrown back over her shoulders, a dark brown kerchief tied over her grey hair, and heavy dark brown boots. On her back she carries one huge overloaded pack, taller than her head and wider than her shoulders, held on by two leather straps over her shoulders: tied onto it are two dented brass cooking pots, a blackened iron pan, an unlit iron lantern, cold, with no flame and no glow, and a rolled grey blanket across the top.
holds: She holds exactly one thing: in her right hand, held out toward the viewer at chest height a hand's width from her body, one glass bottle as big as her fist, round-bellied with a bronze foot-ring and a bronze neck band and a cork, filled with bright red liquid. Her left hand grips the shoulder strap of her pack at her chest. The clay pipe is in her mouth, not in her hand.
pose: On two legs, turned three quarters to the viewer, she trudges forward bent under the great pack, one foot stepped forward and the back heel lifted, leaning in toward the viewer with the red bottle held out to sell, the pipe jutting from her grin.
must_show: a wiry old woman in a patched brown travelling cloak
a huge overloaded pack on her back with pots, a lantern and a rolled blanket
a short clay pipe in her mouth
one red potion bottle held out in one hand
